title: AI Exchange: Is This a Gap?
description: Test your committed gap against three checks before you plan anything.

questions.prompt: Paste in your committed gap, the decision waiting on it, and your definition of what "closed" looks like.
questions.placeholder: Bring what you wrote in Name the Gap. Include the gap itself, the decision that is waiting on it, and the definition of closed you wrote in Part 4.
questions.aiContext: This is Sprint 4 of Reframing Problems with AI. The participant is testing whether what they committed to is really a gap, while they still have time to change it. Run three tests and give a verdict on each. First, can it finish the sentence "Until I know this, I can't ___." If you cannot fill the blank from what they wrote, say what is missing. Second, is "closed" observable, or is it a feeling. Name what would make it pointable. Third, is it load-bearing. What would they have to do differently tomorrow if the answer came back the opposite way. If nothing changes, this is not the gap. Name a specific failure before you say anything encouraging, and do not accept a revision that only adds words. A gap does not become load-bearing by being described at greater length. Give a verdict rather than general feedback.
questions.discussionPrompt: Revise anything that failed. Then write two or three sentences on what it pushed on and what you did about it, including anything you decided it was wrong about.
questions.summaryLabel: Your Revised Gap and What Changed
questions.summaryPlaceholder: Write the revised gap, the decision waiting on it, and your definition of closed. Add two or three sentences on what the exchange pushed on and what you did about it.
